headline: 惠斯勒紀錄片登上大銀幕
context: 紀錄片系列 Exhibition on Screen 推出美國畫家惠斯勒（James McNeill Whistler）的新作，搭配泰特英國美術館的惠斯勒特展上映，特展將於 9 月底閉展。惠斯勒除了以名畫《惠斯勒的母親》聞名，也曾控告藝評家羅斯金（John Ruskin）誹謗，最後只獲判一法尋（farthing）的象徵性賠償金。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The latest Exhibition on Screen documentary does a good job balancing the famous scandals with the subtle brilliance of his art Timed to coincide with Tate Britain’s impressive gallery show – which closes at the end of September, so you haven’t long if you’ve missed it so far – this latest from the Exhibition on Screen strand does a fine job in outlining the ins and outs, and ups and downs of this still somewhat divisive artist who, Whistler’s Mother notwithstanding, is still probably most famous for winning a farthing in damages in his “flinging a pot of paint” libel action against John Ruskin. The film assembles the customary lineup of notables including the Tate’s Carol Jacobi, critic Rachel Campbell-Johnston and art historian Stephen Calloway, the latter of whom’s dandyish attire and Colonel Sanders goatee suggests he has very much bought into the Whistler aesthetic. In fact, as all the interviewees are keen to point out, Whistler’s self-constructed persona, always with an eye to making a splash, is as significant an element of his artistic presence as the art itself – even if, as I can’t be alone in thinking, there’s something fundamentally irritating about his southern-genteel attudinising even at a century and a half’s distance. Be that as it may, the film gets to grips with Whistler’s instinctive brilliance as an artist, his natural flair for boundary-pushing and forward-thinking idealism. The big life episodes – his arrival in London, painting his mother, the brouhaha over the Peacock Room , the court case and subsequent bankruptcy – are recounted, but there is impressive detail on the actual art: from the dynamics behind his brooding Wapping picture to the temper tantrums (not his) that made Harmony in Grey and Green, his portrait of the eight-year-old Cicely Alexander so distinctive. And while Whistler’s dealings with the women in his life wouldn’t exactly pass modern-era scrutiny, his pictures of them are genuinely brilliant, with especial attention given to a wonderfully tender sketch of his wife Beatrix , terminally ill in a hotel bedroom. thread_text:
紀錄片系列 Exhibition on Screen 推出美國畫家惠斯勒（James McNeill Whistler）的新作，搭配泰特英國美術館的惠斯勒特展上映，特展將於 9 月底閉展。惠斯勒除了以名畫《惠斯勒的母親》聞名，也曾控告藝評家羅斯金（John Ruskin）誹謗——起因是羅斯金批評他『把一罐顏料砸向觀眾臉上』——最後惠斯勒只獲判一法尋（farthing）的象徵性賠償金，不久後他也一度宣告破產。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 9 月 15 日發佈的報導。
threads_text:
紀錄片系列 Exhibition on Screen，推出了美國畫家惠斯勒（James McNeill Whistler）的最新一部作品，特別搭配泰特英國美術館目前正在展出的惠斯勒特展上映，這場特展將於 9 月底閉展，想去看的人得把握時間。惠斯勒是個評價兩極的畫家，除了以名畫《惠斯勒的母親》聞名，他這個人本身的故事也很戲劇化：他曾經控告藝評家羅斯金（John Ruskin）誹謗，起因是羅斯金批評他的畫作，說他像是『把一罐顏料砸向觀眾臉上』，最後這場官司惠斯勒只拿到一法尋（farthing）的象徵性賠償，不久後他也一度宣告破產。紀錄片訪問了泰特美術館的策展人卡蘿雅各比，以及多位藝評人與藝術史學家，一起梳理惠斯勒充滿爭議、卻也才華洋溢的一生。

本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 9 月 15 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
voice_text: 有一部新的紀錄片，講的是美國畫家惠斯勒。片子特別搭配泰特英國美術館目前正在展出的惠斯勒特展上映，這場特展九月底就要閉展了。惠斯勒除了以一幅畫他母親的名畫聞名，他這個人本身的故事也很戲劇化。他曾經告一位藝評家誹謗，起因是對方批評他的畫，說他像是把一罐顏料砸向觀眾臉上。這場官司最後惠斯勒只拿到象徵性的一點點賠償金，不久後他也一度宣告破產。紀錄片訪問了美術館的策展人和好幾位藝術史學家，一起梳理他這段充滿爭議、卻也才華洋溢的一生。
